<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard AUR `-bin` package that fetches a prebuilt `.deb` from AppFlowy's official GitHub releases and unpacks it. At the top level, only variable assignments are performed: package metadata (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `provides`, `conflicts`), runtime dependencies, and source definitions. There is no `pkgver()` function, no command substitution executing external commands, and no obfuscated or encoded content.

The `source` array references two files from the project's own upstream repository (`https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy`): the raw LICENSE and a prebuilt `.deb` from the official release. Both are pinned to the specific version `0.14.0`. The `b2sums` array provides actual b2 checksums (not `SKIP`), which is good hygiene. The `package()` function (which contains only standard install/extract operations) will not execute during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`. Nothing in the top-level scope or source array would cause genuinely malicious behavior to execute during sourcing.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard -bin package; no malicious code in top-level scope or sources.</summary>
</security_assessment>

This PKGBUILD file for appflowy-bin appears to be a standard Arch Linux package build script with no detected malicious behavior. The package downloads a prebuilt binary from the official AppFlowy GitHub repository releases (https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy/releases/download), which is a legitimate upstream source for this application. The two source files are: (1) the LICENSE file and (2) the AppFlowy binary .deb package. Both sources are from the project's official GitHub account, which is expected for a binary distribution package.

The package() function performs standard packaging operations: extracting the data.tar.xz from the downloaded .deb file, installing the license to the appropriate location, fixing the desktop entry icon reference, installing the application icon, and creating a symlink to the binary. There are no suspicious network requests, obfuscated code, or unexpected system modifications. The code does not use dangerous commands like eval, curl|bash patterns, or base64 decoding to execute arbitrary code. The b2sums checksums are provided for both sources (not SKIPped), and the operations only touch the package's own files, not system files outside its scope.
</details>
